title: Repairing Damage on the Green
question: On the putting green, which types of damage can you repair without penalty?
explanation: You are permitted to fix pitch-marks, spike marks, and old hole plugs, but not aeration holes or natural imperfections.

juniorVersion.title: Fixing Damage on the Green
juniorVersion.question: When your ball is on the putting green, which things are you allowed to fix before you putt?

choices.text: Marks made by a ball hitting the green or someone’s shoes (pitch-marks and spike marks)
Holes made by special tools to help the grass get air (aeration holes)
Old holes that were used for the flag before (old hole plugs)
Bumpy spots or dips that have always been there (natural imperfections)

juniorVersion.explanation: You can fix places where a ball or shoe made a mark, and old flagstick holes. But you can’t fix air holes or bumpy spots that have always been there.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A dent in the ground made when a ball lands on the green.
A small mark or scratch made by someone’s shoes on the green.
A tiny hole made by a tool to help grass breathe and grow.
The spot where the hole for the flag used to be on the green.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Ask children to show you which marks on the green they think they are allowed to fix before they putt.
likelyMisconceptions: Children may think they can fix any funny spot on the green.
They might try to fix holes made by special tools or bumpy areas from nature.
